_meta.description: Sanctioned skips for yadgar test suite. Every skip must appear here or CI gate fails.

entries.note: Engine-#2 car C. sqlalchemy/asyncmy live in the `sql` extra; Dockerfile.ci:116 bakes only `--extra test --extra ml` and yadgar-ci has no auto-sync pipeline, so these skip until that image is rebuilt with `--extra sql`. Covers the same importorskip in yadgar/tests/integration/test_mariadb_connection.py. The credential half (test_mariadb_option_file.py) and the wiring half (test_mariadb_composition.py) are pure stdlib and never skip.

Engine-#2 car D. alembic travels with sqlalchemy/asyncmy in the `sql` extra; Dockerfile.ci:116 bakes only `--extra test --extra ml` and yadgar-ci has no auto-sync pipeline, so the Alembic-chain tests skip until that image is rebuilt with `--extra sql`. Separate pattern from engine2-sql-extra-absent-01 because the two importorskips name different modules and either can be the one that is missing. Covers the same importorskip in yadgar/tests/integration/test_mariadb_migrations.py. The wiring half (yadgar/tests/backend/test_engine2_migration_wiring.py) is pure stdlib plus stubs and never skips.

Engine-#2 car H (the cross-engine check_invariants arm). The live half reads a real alembic_version stamp and a real config row count, so it needs alembic AND sqlalchemy from the `sql` extra; Dockerfile.ci:116 bakes only `--extra test --extra ml` and yadgar-ci has no auto-sync pipeline. The second importorskip in the same file ('sqlalchemy not installed (sql extra)') is covered by engine2-sql-extra-absent-01. The offline half (yadgar/tests/backend/test_cross_engine_invariants.py) is pure stdlib plus stubs and NEVER skips - which matters more here than elsewhere: this car exists to kill vacuous passes, so its own coverage must not evaporate when an extra is missing.
R6 bounded-wall-clock test needs coreutils `timeout`; absent on macOS hosts, where the linger helper is a no-op anyway (no logind)
Requires live DB and YADGAR_TEST_LIVE_SCAN=1 env var; CI does not set this
launchd install — macOS-only feature; covers all 3 macOS skips in this file
uninstall launchd cleanup path — macOS-only feature, cannot run on Linux CI
podman machine socket resolution — macOS-only feature, cannot run on Linux CI
cyclonedx-bom is in [dist]/[sbom] optional extras, not [test] — CI does not install it
test requires shellcheck binary; CI image (python:3.14-slim) does not include it
T7 — investigation showed backend does not require YADGAR_DB_USER; test body is pass by design

Regen-on-demand skip by design. Fixture committed at yadgar/tests/backend/fixtures/causal_discovery_expected.json (Car 2: generated INSIDE the yadgar-ci container — scipy FP sensitivity across BLAS builds). Regenerate only inside the CI container; command in the test module docstring.
duckdb is an optional dep not included in [test] extras or CI image (python:3.14-slim). All 18 duckdb skips are covered by this entry.
nix binary absent in CI container; flake checks run on dev machines (NixOS). Stays a skip — nix-in-container is unreasonable weight.
Regen-on-demand skip by design. Fixture committed at yadgar/tests/core/fixtures/retrieval_core_expected.json.
Linked-worktree detection tests build a real git repo + worktree fixture; skipped only where git is absent (never in CI — checkout requires git)

entries.reason_pattern: real-model load smoke — opt-in via YADGAR_MODEL_LOAD_SMOKE=1
entries.note: Deps-train gates b/c/d: downloads real model weights (Ettin/GTE/MiniLM/doc2query) and runs real inference — opt-in local pre-merge gate, never runs in CE-mocked CI legs. Covers the module-level skipif. The flashrank importorskip this note used to sanction was removed with the flashrank CE tier (ADR-0191, task 0121): flashrank was never in pyproject/uv.lock, so that case never executed in any gate.

entries.reason_pattern: codebase-memory-mcp binary not installed (live smoke; mirrors conftest.py:491 surreal guard)
entries.note: code_graph Car B (ADR-0162) live smoke: the codebase-memory-mcp static binary is a 259MB host-side external dep installed opt-in via `yadgar setup --code-graph`, never present in CI. Unit coverage fully mocks subprocess/git; this class asserts the real binary resolves when installed. Mirrors the conftest.py surreal shutil.which guard pattern.

entries.reason_pattern: codebase-memory-mcp binary not installed (Car F live e2e; mirrors conftest.py:491 surreal guard)
entries.note: code_graph Car F (ADR-0162) end-to-end smoke: builds a hermetic throwaway git repo with a local bare origin, drives the real `yadgar code-graph refresh --json` seam against the real 259MB codebase-memory-mcp binary, and asserts a bounded non-empty digest + emit-payload shape. The binary is an opt-in host-side dep (`yadgar setup --code-graph`), never in CI — module-level skipif covers both e2e classes. Mirrors the conftest.py surreal shutil.which guard pattern. task:0067 extends this module with a real-binary stale-marker confirmation (index once, break the origin URL so `git fetch` fails, assert the cached digest is re-emitted with `stale @ <sha>` and reason `fetch_failed`); it inherits the SAME module-level pytestmark and reason string, so this entry sanctions it and no duplicate row is needed — sanctioning is substring-matched on reason_pattern, not per-test. That stale assertion is belt-and-braces only: the load-bearing CI-VISIBLE coverage is `test_code_graph_cli.py::TestDispatch::test_refresh_reemits_stale_marked_digest_on_fetch_failure`, which needs no binary.

systemd-analyze calendar is the only real (non-string-match) validation that the rendered OnCalendar expressions parse and elapse; the binary is absent on macOS hosts and minimal CI images, where the render assertions still run

nix-flake detection requires a real path literally prefixed /nix/store/, which cannot be synthesized under tmp_path — the check-in-store fixture (a symlink to the test host's own nix-built bash) only exists on real NixOS/nix-installed hosts. The CI test-fast job runs in a plain ubuntu-based container with no /nix/store, so this one parity case skips there; the other 7 (pipx legacy/modern/explicit-PIPX_HOME/false-positive, brew, source, unknown) are pure tmp_path fixtures and always run.

entries.reason_pattern: no working container runtime on this host
entries.note: Engine-#2 car F. The dump arm's integration test spins a scratch MariaDB container to prove the real argv + credential path; no working container runtime means no server to dump. Mirrors the same guard in yadgar/tests/integration/test_mariadb_connection.py (car C). Torn down with -v so no anonymous datadir volume leaks. Car G5: message changed from presence-only ("docker/podman not available on this host") to a functional-probe result ("no WORKING container runtime") — the self-hosted runner carries a podman binary that is present but non-functional (rootless podman cannot nest inside the runner's own container), so a presence check alone no longer describes what actually happened.

entries.reason_pattern: mariadb-dump not available on this host
entries.note: Engine-#2 car F. In production the dump runs INSIDE the backend container, where the mariadb-server apt install (Dockerfile.backend) provides mariadb-dump; a host running this integration test needs the client binary locally. Distinct from engine2-sql-extra-absent-01: this arm shells a binary and imports nothing from the `sql` extra, so the yadgar-ci --extra sql rebuild does not fix it.

Engine-#2 cars C and F. Both MariaDB integration tests skip rather than fail when `podman/docker run` itself errors (image not pulled, no network, rootless storage full) — the runtime is present but cannot produce a server, which is an environment fault and not a yadgar regression. Also covers the identical guard in yadgar/tests/integration/test_mariadb_connection.py, which predates this entry. Car G's yadgar/tests/integration/test_mariadb_restore_arm.py carries the same three guards.

entries.reason_pattern: no working container runtime on this host
entries.note: Engine-#2 car G. The restore arm's integration test is the ONLY evidence exit criterion 4 holds — a deliberately partial restore is rejected — and it needs a real server to replay a dump into a scratch schema and enumerate it row-for-row. No working container runtime means no server. Same guard shape as car F's dump arm. Torn down with -v so no anonymous datadir volume leaks. Car G5: message changed from presence-only to a functional-probe result — see engine2-carf-container-runtime-absent-01's note for why.

entries.reason_pattern: mariadb client not available on this host
entries.note: Engine-#2 car G. DISTINCT from engine2-carf-mariadb-client-absent-01: that one names `mariadb-dump`, this one names the `mariadb` CLIENT, and a host can have either without the other. The restore arm shells the client both to replay the artifact and to run the enumeration queries; in production it ships with the mariadb-server apt install baked into Dockerfile.backend. Like car F it imports nothing from the `sql` extra, so the yadgar-ci --extra sql rebuild does not fix it.
